court: Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of the State of New York

issues.label: Proper court jurisdiction/venue
issues.why: The court must confirm it is the proper forum to classify the defendant under SORA for the convictions at issue.

issues.label: Timeliness before release
issues.why: The court must ensure the SORA hearing and order were timely in anticipation of release from incarceration.

issues.label: Applicable SORA version
issues.why: The court must apply the correct statutory and guideline provisions in effect for the classification proceeding.

issues.label: Record includes all convictions
issues.why: The court must determine what convictions and conduct may be considered (Sullivan-only RAI vs global criminal history including Queens matters).

issues.label: RAI scoring correctness
issues.why: The court must verify each RAI factor was scored correctly and supported by reliable evidence.

issues.label: Presumptive level determination
issues.why: The court must confirm that 100 points yields presumptive risk level two under the Guidelines.

issues.label: Burden for RAI points
issues.why: The court must ensure the People met the clear-and-convincing evidence standard for assessed RAI points.

issues.label: Reliable hearsay admissibility
issues.why: The court must decide what documentary/hearsay materials are admissible and whether they are sufficiently reliable for SORA purposes.

issues.label: Defendant’s due process rights
issues.why: The court must ensure notice of the proposed level/departure, access to evidence, and an opportunity to be heard and contest the proof.

issues.label: Counsel right and effectiveness
issues.why: The court must ensure defendant had counsel and a meaningful chance to litigate scoring/departure issues.

issues.label: Departure framework applied
issues.why: The court must apply the correct two-step departure analysis required by the Guidelines and case law.

issues.label: Identify departure aggravators
issues.why: The court must specify the precise aggravating factor(s) asserted to justify an upward departure.

issues.label: Factor not adequately captured
issues.why: The court must determine whether the asserted aggravator is not otherwise adequately accounted for by the RAI.

issues.label: Second victim proof
issues.why: The court must decide whether there is clear and convincing proof of a distinct second underage victim, not merely additional charges or duplicative allegations.

issues.label: Distinct victim vs same victim
issues.why: The court must resolve whether the Queens and Sullivan conduct involved one victim or multiple victims given overlap described.

issues.label: Use of Queens case facts
issues.why: The court must determine whether, and to what extent, facts from the Queens informations may be used to support departure when the RAI covered only Sullivan offenses.

issues.label: Use of unscored convictions
issues.why: The court must decide whether separate convictions not scored on the RAI can justify departure and under what evidentiary basis.

issues.label: Non-element conduct reliance
issues.why: The court must ensure any reliance on conduct beyond elements of conviction is supported by reliable evidence and properly considered under SORA standards.

issues.label: Avoid double counting
issues.why: The court must ensure the same facts are not used both to score RAI points and again to justify an upward departure.

issues.label: Magnitude of departure
issues.why: The court must determine whether the proven aggravators warrant moving from level two to level three as a reasonable exercise of discretion.

issues.label: Discretion and balancing
issues.why: The court must balance aggravating and mitigating circumstances and explain why a departure is warranted in light of the totality of circumstances.

issues.label: Consider mitigating factors
issues.why: The court must consider any mitigating factors raised (e.g., treatment, age, time offense-free, medical issues) and whether they warrant no departure or a lesser level.

issues.label: Procedural notice of departure grounds
issues.why: The court must ensure the defendant received adequate pre-hearing notice of the specific upward-departure grounds (e.g., second victim) to prepare a defense.

issues.label: Adequacy of court findings
issues.why: The court must make specific findings of fact and conclusions supporting both the presumptive score and the upward departure.

issues.label: Written order compliance
issues.why: The court must ensure the SORA order and level determination comply with statutory requirements and are properly recorded.

issues.label: Special designation consideration
issues.why: The court must consider whether any special designations (e.g., sexual predator, sexually violent offender) were sought/required and make appropriate findings or note their absence.

issues.label: Standard of appellate review
issues.why: The court must recognize that scoring is reviewed for clear-and-convincing support and departures for proper legal analysis and abuse of discretion, shaping what must be established.

issues.label: Scope of risk assessment evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether the hearing record supports findings beyond the RAI, including probation/PSI, victim statements, and other official documents.

issues.label: Effect of global resolution
issues.why: The court must determine whether the global plea/sentence impacts what underlying conduct may be considered for risk and departure analysis.

issues.label: Multiplicity/overlap of offenses
issues.why: The court must account for overlap between counties to avoid treating the same victim/episode as separate aggravating circumstances.

issues.label: Risk level consequences accuracy
issues.why: The court must ensure the classification level chosen aligns with statutory/community-notification consequences and is legally supportable given the findings.
